title: The unanimous Declaration of the thirteen united States of America
author: Thomas Jefferson and the Second Continental Congress
note: The full text; public domain as a US government work of 1776.

title: 南國山河
author: anonymous (traditionally attributed to Lý Thường Kiệt)
note: The complete four-line poem in the original Chinese characters (the typographic spaces between characters in the Wikisource table were removed; the main reading 定分 is used); an 11th-century anonymous text, public domain.

title: Nam quốc sơn hà
author: anonymous (traditionally attributed to Lý Thường Kiệt)
note: Only the four-line Sino-Vietnamese reading: the verse translation 'Sông núi nước Nam vua Nam ở' is attributed to Trần Trọng Kim (d. 1953) in secondary web sources but could not be found in any public-domain edition read (his Việt Nam sử lược on Wikisource quotes only the Sino-Vietnamese reading), so it was omitted; the reading of an 11th-century text is public domain.

title: Ազատություն
author: Mikael Nalbandian
note: The complete poem in six eight-line stanzas; Nalbandian died in 1866, so the text is public domain.

title: Nocturne
author: Eino Leino
note: The complete poem (three ten-line stanzas) from Talvi-yö; Leino died in 1926, so the text is public domain.

title: Kalevala, ensimmäinen runo
author: Elias Lönnrot (compiler), Finnish oral tradition
note: The opening of the first poem of the 1849 Kalevala, 51 lines (Mieleni minun tekevi ... uuen aamun alkeheksi); Lönnrot died in 1884, public domain.

title: Qaro ko‘zum
author: Alisher Navoiy
note: The complete ghazal of eight couplets ('Qaro ko‘zum, kel-u, mardumliq emdi fan qilg‘il', radif 'qilg‘il', takhallus Navoiy in the last couplet) in Uzbek Latin script from the multilingual Wikisource; Navoiy died in 1501, so the text is public domain.

title: Carmen V
author: Gaius Valerius Catullus
note: The complete 13-line poem from the F. W. Cornish edition (1904, Cornish d. 1916) with marginal line numbers removed; an ancient text, public domain.

title: いろは歌
author: anonymous
note: The complete 47-kana pangram in historical kana spelling, followed after a blank line by its traditional kanji-and-kana rendering as given on the same page; an anonymous Heian-period text, public domain.

title: Я вас любил: любовь ещё, быть может…
author: Alexander Pushkin
note: The complete eight-line poem; Pushkin died in 1837, so the text is public domain.

title: Ἰλιάς Α
author: Homer
note: The opening 21 lines (proem and the priest Chryses' plea) from the Monro–Allen Oxford text (1920, Allen d. 1950) with marginal line numbers removed; an ancient text, public domain.

title: תהלים כג
author: traditional (attributed to David)
note: The complete six-verse psalm in the Masoretic text with niqqud and te'amim, verse numerals removed and each verse as a stanza; an ancient text, public domain.

title: 訓民正音 (나랏〮말〯ᄊᆞ미〮)
author: King Sejong the Great
script: Hangul (15th-century Old Hangul with tone marks and some Hanja)
note: The eight-clause Korean preface of the Hunminjeongeum eonhae (Worin seokbo edition of 1459) in its original Old Hangul with side-dot tone marks, excluding the interlinear glosses; a 15th-century text, public domain.

title: ვეფხისტყაოსანი
titleLatin: Vepkhistqaosani (The Knight in the Panther's Skin), prologue 1–6
author: Shota Rustaveli
note: The first six quatrains of the prologue, stanza numbers removed; a 12th-century text, public domain.

title: El ingenioso hidalgo Don Quijote de la Mancha
titleLatin: Don Quixote, Part I, chapter I (opening)
author: Miguel de Cervantes
note: The first paragraph of chapter I from the 1905 edition (with its orthography, e.g. 'á'); Cervantes died in 1616, so the text is public domain.

title: भगवद्गीता २.४५–५०
author: traditional (attributed to Vyasa)
note: Verses 2.45 to 2.50 (including 2.47 karmaṇy evādhikāras te), each verse a two-line stanza with verse numerals removed; an ancient text, public domain.

title: Völuspá
author: anonymous
note: The first ten stanzas in Sophus Bugge's 1867 text in normalized spelling, stanza numbers removed; a medieval anonymous text, public domain.

title: معلقة امرئ القيس
author: Imru' al-Qais
note: The first ten verses (qifā nabki), each verse a two-line stanza with the two hemistichs on separate lines; a pre-Islamic text, public domain.
